parts.html: The K-42 kitchen is a modern L-shaped kitchen: light, creamy beige wall cabinets and dark blue lower fronts. The tall sections on the right are the same blue: they add a vertical element and close off the kitchen.
The light top keeps the kitchen from feeling heavy, and the rich blue is concentrated below and in the tall sections.
On the right, between the tall sections, there are built-in open vertical shelves for dishes, decor, and small things you like to keep in sight. All other storage is closed.
The very dark countertop draws a crisp horizontal line against the light backsplash. The backsplash has a vertical relief, but its color is neutral, so it does not compete with the blue.
The black faucet and built-in appliances pick up the dark countertop and the blue base.
Layout
The furniture runs along two adjoining walls, and the corner is used too. The countertop, cabinets, and built-in appliances are spread over two sides, so each zone has its own place.
It is 4.8 linear meters long; the standard model measures 4.8 × 2.4 × 0.6 m.

In the visualization, the work run continues into the corner, and on the right stand tall cabinets with a built-in oven and open shelves. The countertop and the tall block together make up one kitchen.

The K-42 has spaces planned in advance for built-in appliances; which appliances go where is decided during the design stage, taking utility connections into account. The cost of the appliances themselves is not included in the furniture price.
A kitchen island is not included in the standard K-42 configuration.
Front materials and finishes
All the fronts are laminated chipboard: creamy beige on top, dark blue below and on the tall sections on the right.
The cabinet carcasses are 18 mm laminated chipboard.
The countertop is chipboard-based; in the visualization it has a very dark, almost black decor.
Hardware and storage systems
The K-42 already has a cargo system: food and small kitchen items go in a pull-out section.
The hinged fronts have Hettich soft-close hinges.
The drawers run on Quadro Hettich concealed undermount slides: the mechanism sits under the drawer and cannot be seen from outside.
Cabinet handles are included in the standard configuration.
The wall cabinets have no lift-up mechanisms.
